미안합니다.x: Sorry I'm late. The traffic was really bad.
미안합니다.e: Literally 'not at ease' + 합니다 — I feel uneasy about what I did.
미안합니다.t: With elders, bosses or customers, 죄송합니다 is safer and more respectful.

평일.x: On weekdays I go to work.
평일.e: Literally 'ordinary day' — the opposite of 주말 (weekend).

종류.x: This shop has many kinds of bread.
종류.e: Literally 'kind + type'. 무슨 종류? = what kind?
종류.t: Pronounced [종뉴]: ㄹ after ㅇ becomes ㄴ.

맑다.t: Pronounced [막따], but 맑아요 [말가요] — the ㄹ comes back before a vowel.

궁금하다.ex: 그 영화가 어떻게 끝나는지 정말 궁금해요.
궁금하다.x: I'm really curious how that movie ends.
궁금하다.e: 궁금한 점, 'a point you're curious about,' is how Koreans often say 'a question'.
궁금하다.t: Teachers say 궁금한 거 있으면 물어보세요, 'If you're curious about anything, ask,' all the time.

읽기.m: reading (as a skill or test section)
읽기.x: Reading is easier for me than listening.
읽기.e: Verb 읽다 'to read' plus noun-making -기; same for 쓰기, 듣기, 말하기.
읽기.t: Pronounced [일끼]; TOPIK sections are 듣기, 읽기 and 쓰기.

통화하다.m: to talk on the phone, to speak by phone
통화하다.ex: 어제 친구와 한 시간 동안 통화했어요.
통화하다.x: I talked on the phone with my friend for an hour yesterday.
통화하다.t: Use N하고/N와 통화하다 'talk on the phone with N'.

청소년.ex: 이 영화는 청소년이 볼 수 없습니다.
청소년.x: Teenagers are not allowed to see this movie.
청소년.e: Literally 'green, young years' — youth in its fresh stage.

끝.ex: 영화 끝에 정말 슬픈 장면이 나와요.
끝.x: There's a really sad scene at the end of the movie.
끝.e: Root of 끝나다 (to end) and 끝내다 (to finish).
끝.t: 끝이 is pronounced [끄치] and 끝을 [끄틀] — ㅌ turns into ㅊ before 이.

병실.x: The hospital room my friend is staying in is on the fifth floor.

역할.ex: 엄마는 우리 집에서 중요한 역할을 해요.
역할.x: Mom plays an important role in our family.
역할.e: Literally 'divided duty': each person's share of the work.
역할.t: Pronounced [여칼]: ㄱ followed by ㅎ becomes ㅋ.

상하다.m: to go bad, to spoil; to be hurt, to be damaged
상하다.x: The milk has gone bad, so it smells strange.
상하다.e: Literally 'to be harmed': food gets spoiled, feelings get hurt.
상하다.t: With feelings, 기분이 상했어요 means 'My feelings were hurt.'

측면.ex: 이 문제는 여러 측면에서 생각해 봐야 해요.
측면.x: We need to think about this problem from several angles.
측면.t: Pronounced [층면] — nasalization turns ㄱ into ㅇ before ㅁ.

정보화.m: informatization, the shift to an information society
정보화.ex: 정보화 시대에는 컴퓨터를 잘 다룰 줄 알아야 해요.
정보화.x: In the information age, you need to know how to use a computer well.

공예.ex: 저는 요즘 가죽 공예를 배우고 있어요.
공예.x: These days I'm learning leather craft.
공예.e: Literally 'work art' — art made by hand.

장편.ex: 그 작가의 첫 장편 소설이 큰 인기를 얻었어요.
장편.x: The author's first novel became very popular.

성분.ex: 이 화장품에는 어떤 성분이 들어 있어요?
성분.x: What ingredients are in this cosmetic product?
성분.t: 성분 is what something contains (medicine, cosmetics, labels); cooking ingredients are 재료.

액체.ex: 비행기 안에는 액체를 조금만 가지고 탈 수 있어요.
액체.x: You can only bring a small amount of liquid onto a plane.

그렇다면.m: if so, in that case, then
그렇다면.x: In that case, let's look for another way.

특사.x: The president sent a special envoy to a neighboring country.
특사.t: Homonym: 특사 (特赦) means a 'special pardon' granted by the president.

장려하다.ex: 정부는 출산을 장려하는 정책을 시행하고 있습니다.
장려하다.x: The government is implementing policies that encourage having children.
장려하다.t: Pronounced [장녀하다] — ㄹ after ㅇ becomes ㄴ.

힐끗.ex: 옆자리 사람이 내 휴대폰을 힐끗 쳐다봤어요.
힐끗.x: The person next to me glanced at my phone.
힐끗.e: A mimetic word for a quick sideways look; a variant of 흘끗.
힐끗.t: Repeat it as 힐끗힐끗 for someone glancing again and again.

잠재성.ex: 이 기술은 성장 잠재성이 매우 큽니다.
잠재성.x: This technology has huge growth potential.
잠재성.t: Pronounced [잠재썽]: the suffix -성 is usually tensed.

국고.x: A lot of public money went into that project.
국고.t: Pronounced [국꼬]; often in 국고 낭비 (waste of taxpayers' money).

의존성.ex: 약에 대한 의존성이 생기지 않도록 조심하세요.
의존성.x: Be careful not to develop a dependence on the medicine.
의존성.e: Literally 'nature of relying on something to exist'. -성 = -ness, quality: 가능성, 중요성.

후진국.ex: 그 나라는 수십 년 만에 후진국에서 선진국이 되었습니다.
후진국.x: In a few decades, that country went from underdeveloped to developed.
후진국.t: 후진국 can sound condescending; 개발 도상국 is the neutral term for 'developing country'.

팬데믹.x: Remote work has increased a lot since the pandemic.
팬데믹.t: Official Korean texts often prefer 세계적 대유행 over the loanword 팬데믹.

액운.ex: 새해에 액운을 막으려고 부적을 붙이는 사람도 있어요.
액운.x: Some people put up talismans in the new year to ward off bad luck.

경위서.m: written account of an incident, incident report
경위서.ex: 사고가 난 뒤 담당자는 경위서를 제출해야 합니다.
경위서.x: After an accident, the person in charge must submit an incident report.
경위서.e: 경위 means 'warp and weft' of cloth, hence 'the full details of how it happened'.
경위서.t: A 경위서 explains what happened; a 시말서 also admits fault and is closer to a formal apology.

묵묵부답.x: I asked my brother why he was late, but he said nothing.
묵묵부답.t: Pronounced [뭉묵뿌답]. In news: 묵묵부답으로 일관하다 'to keep refusing to comment'.

근저당.m: maximum-amount mortgage (securing future debts up to a ceiling)
근저당.ex: 이 아파트에는 은행의 근저당이 설정되어 있어요.
근저당.x: This apartment has a bank mortgage registered on it.
근저당.e: 근 'root' plus 저당 'mortgage' — a ceiling-amount mortgage covering future debts.
근저당.t: Before renting a jeonse apartment, check the property register for any 근저당 — a key tenant safety step.

공갈.m: extortion, blackmail, intimidation; (slang) a lie, bluff
공갈.ex: 그는 사업가를 협박해 돈을 뜯어낸 공갈 혐의를 받고 있어요.
공갈.x: He is accused of extortion for threatening a businessman to squeeze money out of him.
공갈.t: In casual speech 공갈 치지 마 means 'Stop lying / bluffing'.

쇄국정책.ex: 쇄국정책 때문에 조선의 근대화가 늦어졌다는 의견도 있어요.
쇄국정책.x: Some argue that the isolationist policy delayed Joseon's modernization.

감지덕지.m: deep gratitude, being thankful for whatever one gets
감지덕지.ex: 요즘 같은 때에 일자리가 있는 것만도 감지덕지예요.
감지덕지.x: In times like these, just having a job is something to be grateful for.
감지덕지.e: Literally 'feel it, count it a blessing' — humble gratitude.
감지덕지.t: Often -만 해도 감지덕지다 'I'd be grateful for even …'; can sound self-deprecating.

빙자하다.m: to use as a pretext, to do under the pretense of
빙자하다.x: He went on a trip under the pretext of a business trip.
빙자하다.e: Literally 'lean on and rely on' — leaning on an excuse.
빙자하다.t: Common pattern: N을/를 빙자하여 or N을/를 빙자한 사기 (fraud).

강건하다.x: My grandfather is over eighty but still strong and healthy.

까마득하다.m: very far off, distant (in time or space); hopeless, at a loss
까마득하다.ex: 학교를 졸업한 게 까마득한 옛날 같아요.
까마득하다.x: Graduating from school feels like ages ago.
까마득하다.e: A stronger cousin of 아득하다 'distant, faint'.
까마득하다.t: Also means 'clueless what to do': 앞날이 까마득해요 'The future looks hopeless.'

신의성실.m: good faith, the principle of good faith and fair dealing
신의성실.ex: 계약 당사자는 신의성실의 원칙에 따라 행동해야 합니다.
신의성실.x: Parties to a contract must act according to the principle of good faith.
신의성실.t: Often shortened to 신의칙 in legal writing.
